questions.q: Why save the entire fitted pipeline instead of only the final classifier?
options: The pipeline carries the learned imputer, scaler, and encoder values, so new raw rows are preprocessed identically
The file is always smaller that way
The classifier alone cannot be saved
joblib refuses to save single estimators
questions.explain: Preprocessing statistics are learned during fit. Saving the whole pipeline keeps them together with the model, so raw rows can be scored without rebuilding the preprocessing.

questions.q: What is the strongest reason not to load a joblib or pickle file downloaded from an unknown source?
options: It will be too large to fit in memory
Loading can execute arbitrary code
It will only work on one operating system
It will always have the wrong feature names
questions.explain: Pickle-based formats can run code while loading, so an untrusted file is as risky as an untrusted script.

questions.q: You upgrade scikit-learn and want to keep using an older saved model. What is the recommended approach?
options: Load it and assume it works, since joblib guarantees compatibility
Delete the metadata so warnings disappear
Retrain from your code and data on the new version, then re-run the evaluation
Rename the file to .pkl
questions.explain: scikit-learn does not guarantee that files saved with one version load correctly or predict identically in another. Retraining and re-evaluating is the safe path.

questions.q: Which check best shows that a reloaded model is truly equivalent to the original?
options: Comparing file sizes
Comparing predict_proba on the same data with np.array_equal, and testing in a fresh Python process
Printing the model to see its name
Checking that the file extension is .joblib
questions.explain: Identical probabilities on the same inputs prove the state was restored, and a fresh process proves the file alone is sufficient.

questions.q: What belongs in a metadata record saved next to a model file?
options: Only the date
The customers' personal records
The full source code of scikit-learn
Library versions, expected feature columns, the training data description, and the headline test score
questions.explain: Versions let you recreate the environment, the feature list defines valid input, and the data and score document what the model is and how it performed.
